items.title: 7.2.2 Measuring the rate of a chemical reaction

source_refs.note: Topic 7.2.2, printed pages 147-148 (Figure 7.2 and Table 7.1), with Quick Check 7.3 as the self-check. The print's '2.5 moles per dm-3 every second' is a slip for 4 x 10^-4.

blocks.text: Measuring the rate of a reaction means determining the concentration of a reactant or product at regular intervals as the reaction progresses. A graph of concentration (y-axis) against time (x-axis) gives a curve. For the decomposition of HI to H2 and I2 at 500 degrees C the data of Table 7.1 give a falling curve, since HI is a reactant. The steepness of the curve reflects the progress of the reaction: the greater the slope near the start, the greater the rate. To measure the rate at, say, 100 seconds, draw a tangent to the curve there and measure its slope: complete a right-angled triangle with the tangent as hypotenuse; in 100 s the concentration changes by 0.04 mol dm-3, so rate = 0.04 / 100 = 4 x 10^-4 mol dm-3 s-1. This means the HI concentration is decreasing by 4 x 10^-4 mol dm-3 every second at that moment (the print says '2.5 moles'). A graph of the concentration of a product, H2 or I2, gives a rising curve whose tangent at 100 s gives the same rate.

blocks.caption: Change in concentration of HI with time, 2HI gives H2 + I2 (Table 7.1)

blocks.prompt: Using Table 7.1, compare the rate at the start, at 100 s and at 300 s, and say at which concentration the rate is highest and lowest.
blocks.explanation: Between 0 and 50 s the concentration falls by 0.0284 mol dm-3, about 5.7 x 10^-4 mol dm-3 s-1; at 100 s the tangent gives 4 x 10^-4; between 250 and 300 s the fall is 0.004 mol dm-3, about 8 x 10^-5 mol dm-3 s-1. The rate is highest at the start, when [HI] is 0.10 mol dm-3, and lowest at 300 s, when it is about 0.03 mol dm-3: the rate falls as the concentration falls.

items: Plot concentration against time; the slope of the tangent at a chosen time is the rate there: HI at 100 s, 0.04 mol dm-3 / 100 s = 4 x 10^-4 mol dm-3 s-1; a product curve gives the same value.
